subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<name>.enabled:false` become a hard read/exec access-deny boundary for that skill directory?
rationale: The current code treats the setting as eligibility and prompt visibility, while hard denial changes a security boundary and could affect existing operator workflows.

options.title: Make disabled skills hard-deny
options.body: Define `enabled:false` as the canonical disabled-skill security boundary and implement one shared enforcement path with docs and tests.

options.title: Add a separate strict policy
options.body: Keep `enabled:false` as eligibility-only and introduce an explicit strict skill-access policy for deployments that need hard isolation.

options.title: Document current semantics
options.body: Leave `enabled:false` as prompt/status filtering and document that sandbox/tool policy, not skill enablement, is the enforcement boundary.

recommendation.title: Make disabled skills hard-deny
recommendation.body: Define `enabled:false` as the canonical disabled-skill security boundary and implement one shared enforcement path with docs and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily a security/product contract choice, and recent adjacent history plus VISION.md security direction point there as the best available owner.
